change: Preallocate straight-line array/fixed-array comprehensions using the existing input snapshot length. Plain results write by stable control index; managed values keep incremental initialized length. Recognize leading straight-line local declarations, including combined index/value loop bindings.

benchmark.compile_conclusion: Netpong, Dunes and compiler CPU times were within 1% in five pairs. Tour initially measured 18% higher paired CPU, but seven fresh pairs with the independent C-bootstrap candidate measured 0.998x; timings shifted markedly within each run. No established compilation improvement or regression claim for that small workload.

coverage: empty dynamic arrays, fixed arrays, contiguous slices and source/bound evaluation order
callbacks clear or replace source; snapshot remains independent
managed nested arrays, dictionary entries and repeated-work allocation cleanup
mutable user index bindings and independent local copies
break, continue and early-return initializers remain on general path
float32/float64 value/indexed-value loop IR uses SIMD in default/release; AVX2 and forced SSE2; lengths 0–19; short second array retains bounds error
limits: Only straight-line bodies with a final collected value; conditional values, nested blocks and loops are conservatively excluded.
Array inputs retain their existing value-snapshot/borrowing behavior; no new borrowing rules.
Named allocation-inclusive kernels, not a general C parity claim.
Fused/range-loop controls varied about 0–5%; no speedup claim for unchanged forms.
validation: Independent C bootstrap and full gate: 5107 passed in 150.82s with two workers. Earlier focused checks: 302 passed in 5.36s. Ruff and git diff --check passed.
